title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of beta-sitosterol on TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53-mediated signaling in the kidney of a high-fat diet and sucrose-induced type-2 diabetic rat.
authors: Jayaraman, Selvaraj; Prasad, Monisha; Natarajan, Sathan Raj; Krishnamoorthy, Rajapandiyan; Alshuniaber, Mohammad A; Gatasheh, Mansour K; Veeraraghavan, Vishnu Priya; Rajagopal, Ponnulakshmi; Palanisamy, Chella Perumal
one_liner_zh: 该文研究β-谷甾醇对糖尿病肾病大鼠TGF-β1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53信号通路的调控，虽含分子对接，但核心是药物-蛋白互作与疾病机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy, a severe problem of diabetes mellitus, is exacerbated by high-fat diets, prompting a need for interventions. Previous study from our laboratory has shown that beta-sitosterol, a potent plant sterol has anti-inflammatory and glucose-lowering efficacy by involving insulin metabolic signalling pathway but its role on anti-oxidant signaling pathways, play a crucial role in mitigating oxidative stress and inflammation associated diabetic nephropathy, highlighting its importance as a potential therapeutic target for managing this debilitating complication of diabetes is unknown. This study was aimed to intricate the molecular mechanisms involved in the potential of beta-sitosterol (BSIT) on TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53 signaling in high fat diet (HFD) and sucrose induced diabetic nephropathy (DN) in the rat kidney by employing various comprehensive bioinformatic analysis. We have used various comprehensive methods such as pathway predictions, Drug-Protein Interaction, Functional annotation analysis, and molecular docking techniques. Further, in vivo analysis of BSIT on biochemical profiles, gene and protein expression analysis of anti-oxidant and inflammatory signaling molecules was performed in the kidney of high fat diet (HFD) and sucrose-induced diabetic nephropathy. Computational studies provided insights into beta-sitosterol's binding affinities and interaction modes with key proteins, suggesting its potential to regulate TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53 signaling pathways. Results of in vivo findings validated computational predictions, showcasing BSIT's multifaceted effects in mitigating diabetic nephropathy and associated complications including regulation of lipid metabolism, combating oxidative stress, and inflammation. The findings underscore BSIT's therapeutic potential by preserving cellular viability, regulating cell death, enhancing antioxidant defence, and stabilizing metabolic processes. Our study concludes that BSIT's ability to potentially regulate TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53 pathways, emphasizing its promising role in managing diabetic nephropathy and associated complications.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病肾病（diabetic nephropathy）是糖尿病的一个严重并发症，高脂饮食会加剧其进展，因此亟需干预措施。我们实验室先前的研究表明，β-谷甾醇（beta-sitosterol）作为一种有效的植物甾醇，通过涉及胰岛素代谢信号通路发挥抗炎和降糖功效，但其对抗氧化信号通路的作用——这些通路在缓解与糖尿病肾病相关的氧化应激和炎症中起关键作用，从而凸显其作为管理这一糖尿病致残性并发症的潜在治疗靶点的重要性——尚不明确。本研究旨在通过采用多种综合性生物信息学分析，阐明β-谷甾醇（BSIT）在高脂饮食（HFD）和蔗糖诱导的大鼠糖尿病肾病（DN）肾脏中对TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53信号通路的潜在分子机制。我们使用了多种综合方法，如通路预测、药物-蛋白质相互作用、功能注释分析以及分子对接技术。此外，在高脂饮食（HFD）和蔗糖诱导的糖尿病肾病大鼠肾脏中，进行了BSIT对生化指标、抗氧化和炎症信号分子的基因及蛋白表达分析的体内研究。计算研究提供了对β-谷甾醇与关键蛋白质结合亲和力及相互作用模式的见解，表明其具有调节TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53信号通路的潜力。体内研究结果验证了计算预测，展示了BSIT在缓解糖尿病肾病及相关并发症（包括调节脂质代谢、对抗氧化应激和炎症）中的多方面效应。这些发现强调了BSIT通过维持细胞活力、调节细胞死亡、增强抗氧化防御和稳定代谢过程来发挥治疗潜力。我们的研究得出结论，BSIT具有潜在调节TGF-beta1/Nrf2/SIRT1/p53通路的能力，强调其在管理糖尿病肾病及相关并发症中的前景作用。
